Both are letters to foreign leaders responding to requests for American assistance; both affirm a desire to promote the recipient country's welfare and stability; and, most distinctively, both propose using an American diplomatic representative to consult with the recipient government about how a program of aid can be made effective. C04 shares the request-and-response structure and economic-development purpose but proceeds directly to enumerated commitments rather than preliminary consultations.
